A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WARP study despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–P are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original membership-inference and reconstruction experiments, alongside privacy–utility, runtime, adaptive-attack and hyperparameter analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–5 and the adaptive-attack and sensitivity experiments in Appendices N and P.

M1.justification: Appendix K, Algorithm 3 removes the additive Gaussian perturbation and its noise-sampling line from the teleportation update. This localized procedural revision aligns the update with the unchanged Equation 8; the objectives, change-of-basis alternative and FastWARP remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation or experiments changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10, Tiny-ImageNet and ImageNet-1K with the same membership-inference, reconstruction and adaptive-attacker scenarios. No dataset, task or evaluated population is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain NGP, SCRUB, PGU, SalUn, SF/SRF-ON and BadTeacher, together with GIFD in Table 3 and the Langevin configurations in Table 5. The new citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported splits, architectures, metrics and attack settings are unchanged. Examples include the approximately 1% forget sets, Section 4.3's 1,000 non-member background samples and ridge parameter of 0.001, and the reconstruction sample counts. No experimental protocol revision is stated alongside the Algorithm 3 edit.

E4.justification: The privacy–utility analysis, runtime and FastWARP comparisons, symmetry-aware adaptive reconstruction attack, and retain-variance/minibatch sensitivity sweeps already appear in v1 and are retained in v2. Their questions and evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the five-split mean and standard-deviation reporting for the ViT evaluation, five-run runtime reporting, and existing uncertainty displays. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: The result entries, plotted findings and numerical discussions match across versions. For example, NGP+WARP's all-sample black-box AUC remains 0.516 in Table 1, and its reconstruction PSNR remains 7.38 ± 0.40 in Table 2. Relocated appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal attack definitions and Appendix O's assumptions, propositions, theorems, corollaries and proofs are retained. Correcting 'betwen' to 'between' in Lemma 1's explanatory sentence does not change mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same privacy attacks, symmetry-based defense and claimed privacy gains. WARP was already named in v1; promoting it into the title does not redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and qualifications remain unchanged, including the SCRUB low-FPR exception, the limits of the Langevin comparison, the deferred LLM application, and Appendix O's distinction between improved analytic bounds and unproved ordering of true reconstruction errors.

D1.justification: v2 adds a statement that the implementation is publicly available and supplies a repository link in Introduction footnote 2; v1 provides neither. The other implementation, hardware and runtime information is retained. The linked resource itself is not verified by the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zk-apex and Telesparse by Maheri et al. to the bibliography, citing them in the threat-model distinction and neural-network symmetry discussion, respectively. It also adds an existing Bourtoule et al. citation to the threat-model passage. These are limited citation additions without a broader positioning rewrite.

P1.justification: The title becomes 'WARP: Weight Teleportation for Attack-Resilient Unlearning Protocols.' v2 also adds a correspondence footnote, code-availability sentence and acknowledgments, and fixes a spelling error. The section sequence and substantive narrative remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Running headers, spacing and pagination change, with some appendix displays relocated: Figure 5 moves from page 17 to 18, while Table 3 moves from page 18 to 17. The existing figure content, captions and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 provides code-access information and removes Algorithm 3's extra Gaussian term, improving consistency with Equation 8. These are limited reproducibility and clarity gains rather than stronger scientific evidence. The correction remains incomplete because Algorithm 3 still lists the unused noise parameter sigma^2; the results and theory are unchanged.
